title: HB2416 (2023 Regular): Relating to extreme risk protection orders.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Oregon) (gun-policy Stage 5, Oregon); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Oregon text (Introduced, official copy, https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2023R1/Downloads/MeasureDocument/HB2416/Introduced; sha256 f16ce88a9a14eb27b8e7e873b607d286756f8762f3851285d0b05fd18a9a9da8)
provenance.note: Introduced version (as filed). The text strikes the one-year duration of the order and the respondent's right to request a termination hearing (ORS 166.533 and 166.535 are repealed in section 8). Sections 5 to 7 conform ORS 166.537, 166.540 and 166.543 and are not quoted. Added words are not marked in the text; quoted passages are those the digest points to. No votes recorded.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (ORS 166.527): (c) The court shall schedule a hearing under ORS 166.530 to occur seven days after issuing an order under this section, and shall further order that the respondent appear at the hearing and obtain a mental health evaluation prior to the hearing.
SECTION 2 (ORS 166.530): (C) Schedule a hearing under section 4 of this 2023 Act to occur seven days after the date of the hearing described in this section, and further order that the respondent appear at the hearing and obtain a second mental health evaluation prior to the hearing.
SECTION 4 (new): (3)(a) At the hearing, the court shall determine: (A) Whether to terminate the extreme risk protection order or continue the order for an additional 30 days; and (B) Whether any deadly weapons surrendered to a law enforcement agency pursuant to ORS 166.537 shall be returned to the respondent or retained by the law enforcement agency.
SECTION 4 (new): (b) The petitioner has the burden of proving, by clear and convincing evidence, that the respondent presents a substantial risk of harm to self or others to such a serious level that it is necessary to temporarily prohibit the respondent from possessing deadly weapons for an additional 30 days.
SECTION 4 (new): (7) The refusal by a respondent to participate in a mental health evaluation or the failure of a respondent to appear at a hearing described in this section is not the basis for a finding of contempt of court.
